title: How an LED Light Bulb Works in 60 Seconds 💡⚡ #shorts
description:
An LED bulb makes light without a glowing hot wire. Inside, a driver turns mains power into low DC, and electrons crossing a tiny semiconductor chip release their energy as light. A yellow phosphor turns the blue light white. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#led #howitworks #shorts

steps.label: The Secret
steps.text: Old bulbs heat a wire until it glows. An *LED* makes light from a chip smaller than a grain of rice.

steps.label: The Driver
steps.text: In the base, a small *driver* circuit turns wall power into low, steady direct current.

steps.label: The Chip
steps.text: The current flows into a *semiconductor* chip with two layers, one with extra electrons, one with holes.

steps.label: Light
steps.text: When an electron drops into a hole, it releases its energy as a tiny flash of *light*.

steps.label: White Light
steps.text: The chip glows *blue*. A yellow phosphor coating mixes it into white light.

steps.label: Efficiency
steps.text: Little energy is wasted as heat, so LEDs need *far less power*.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Driver, chip, electrons, *light*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
